query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the powder feed rate in the HVAF‐i7 operation will compensate for the lower throughput compared to the HVAF‐M3 process, resulting in a thicker yet similarly high‐quality FeCoNiCrAl bond coat while preserving its adhesion, minimal in-spray oxidation, and high-temperature durability even on substrates with internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a particle size distribution of 15–45 μm, used in HVAF-i7 deposition under existing settings that yield acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
generation.intervention: Increase the powder feed rate during the HVAF‐i7 spray process without altering the powder particle size or other core process parameters.
generation.conditions: Deposition using the HVAF-i7 torch on substrates (including those with internal diameters as small as 120 mm) under controlled gas flow and inert atmosphere conditions; standard spray distance (maintained as in current HVAF-i7 operation) with the only variable being the adjusted feed rate.
generation.structural_mediator: A higher flux of powder particles will lead to an increased volume of deposited material per unit time, thereby building up a thicker coating; the in-flight kinetic energy and splat formation remain governed by the unchanged gas dynamics ensuring continued bond integrity.
generation.mechanism: By delivering more powder per unit time into the flame, a greater mass accumulates on the substrate. Given that the HVAF-i7 process already produces acceptable splat formation and adhesion, this extra feed compensates for the lower overall deposition efficiency (compared to HVAF-M3) so that the buildup reaches the desired thickness without compromising the microstructural quality or increasing oxidation significantly.
generation.predicted_outcome: Coatings produced with the increased feed rate will exhibit a significantly greater thickness (approaching that obtained with optimal HVAF-M3 settings) while retaining comparable adhesion, low in-spray oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
generation.baseline: The HVAF-i7 process using the standard powder feed rate (with 15–45 μm feedstock) yields coatings that are of acceptable quality but insufficient in thickness relative to the performance of HVAF-M3 coatings.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective under the HVAF-i7 operating window with its inherent gas dynamics; however, excessive increases in feed rate may risk particle interferences, reduced melting uniformity, or localized in-flight collisions, which could degrade coating integrity. The approach is intended for deposition on substrates with internal diameters down to 120 mm, and its effectiveness must be balanced against potential issues in confined geometries.
generation.uncertainty: While conventional MCrAlY bond coat studies (Query statement, Conventional MCrAlY studies) indicate that higher kinetic energy (linked to particle velocity) improves deposition efficiency, it remains untested whether a higher powder mass flux alone (without modifying velocity or spray distance) can overcome the thickness limitation on the HVAF-i7 system. There is uncertainty regarding the interplay between increased powder concentration and potential effects on particle melting and oxidation.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a controlled deposition study using the HVAF-i7 torch on identical substrate geometries (including substrates with 120 mm internal diameters) while varying only the powder feed rate. Include at least three groups: (1) standard feed rate (baseline), (2) moderately increased feed rate, and (3) significantly increased feed rate. All other deposition parameters (spray distance, gas composition, torch settings) will be held constant. Evaluate the resulting coatings for thickness, microstructural integrity, adhesion, and degree of as-sprayed oxidation.
measurements: Coating thickness (measured via cross-sectional microscopy or profilometry)
Oxide content/oxidation level (using EDS or XRD analysis)
Microstructure quality (using SEM to assess splat formation and porosity)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coatings produced with increased powder feed rates do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in thickness compared to the baseline (without degradation of adhesion or an unacceptable increase in oxidation) or if the higher feed rate causes detrimental defects (poor splat bonding, increased porosity, or compromised microstructure), then the hypothesis will be falsified.
